- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g. +5%+ in 3–5 days) followed by true price drop, suppress next forecast peak by 10–15% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.1) and model forecasts high volatility, reduce forecast magnitude by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- When true price deviates from model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = previous true + 0.5×(true - forecast) if trend is diverging.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overpredicts by 2–4% in recent 5–7 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days to align with sentiment-driven correction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g. -0.5 to -0.7) followed by model overreaction, apply lag correction: forecast = true - 0.3×(forecast - true) for next 3–5 days.
